intent_and_evidence: Keep persistence calls (find/persist/merge/query) out of the business layer behind a small entity-oriented API. Evidence: AccountDAO/UserDAO wrap entityManager.find/persist/merge/createQuery; services call only DAO methods and never reference EntityManager (grep C2); DAO<T> declares the shared findById/getAll contract, but save/update exist only on the concrete DAOs, so services inject the concrete classes (weakened abstraction). Tests replace the EntityManager by an in-memory fake without touching production code.

intent_and_evidence: Decouple the JSON request contract from the persistence entities and carry only the needed fields across the REST boundary. intent_and_evidence: Provide one application boundary that exposes the use cases and coordinates DAOs and converters for the controllers. Evidence: Controllers call only AccountService/UserService; AccountService.createAccount coordinates userService.getUserDetails, accountUtil.convertToAccount and accountDAO.save. Deviation: transaction demarcation is on DAO methods, not on the service operations.

Implement each use case as one procedure that applies the business rules directly to row-like data. Evidence: Rules are inline in the service methods: amount > 0 (AccountService line 43), savings bonus += 0.5 (lines 46-48), withdraw allowed only if amount > 0 && balance > amount (line 67). Account contains only accessors (grep C9), i.e. an anemic entity.

Receive HTTP system events and hand them to the business layer without business logic in the HTTP layer. Evidence: Each controller method unwraps the DTO, makes exactly one service call and wraps the result in a Response (grep C5); no DAO or EntityManager reference in rest/ (grep C1).
